links.reason: 1215 is a request addressed to envoys (வம்மினே) and 1224 only says the foe-kings keep மானம் though they know ruin (ஊனம்); nothing in 1224 ties them to the 1215 ultimatum, so 'answer' and 'told to bow' are supplied. Sense of 1215 is flagged uncertain.

83 sends the minister (மந்திரி தன்னை ஏவ) and 85 gives his speech, a real sequence, but 85 ends பயந்து சென்றான், withdrawal from fear of the one man who destroyed the army, not counsel winning him; the teaches overstates.

Ainkurunuru 159 asks he 'give back' (தந்தனை சென்மோ) with no speaker named; Kuruntokai 349 (கொள்வாம் என்றி தோழி ... கொடுத்தவை தாவென் சொல்லினும்) is a different woman in a different case and its last clause is ambiguous. Different situations, not incompatible claims about one thing.
267 has the fall; 268 says only கண்டனன், the sage sees him, not a rescue; 'start of his rise' is not in either verse. Story sequence, with both verses flagged uncertain.

498 does divide duty (தாங்கல் கடனாகும் ... நீங்கல் மடவார்கள் கடன்) and 'upholding the line' matches ஆண்மை of 1026, but 1026 is about ruling one's own house, and 'voyage as family duty' is the marker's reading of a verse flagged uncertain; the Kural gains nothing real.
1072 (drums, incense, flowers) and 1082 (jewels, gems, cloth) are neighbouring items of one festival description; no distinctive image is shared and the 'build-up' is only order.

325 sits in கள்ளுண்ணாமை and uses drink (சுத்த மதுவுண்ண) for yogic bliss, whose last line is obscure; 2074 gives light, sandal coolness and scent for a Jain state. Shared topic of bliss only; the 'qualifies' and both gains clauses (calmer images, bliss from sitting to lying) are not in either text.

2204's simile is only that the arrows are straight (திண்சரம்) like refined minds; it does not claim form proves worth, and 'starts a war of slaughter' is outside the verse. Kural 279 (கணை கொடிது ... செவ்விது) judges by deed; no incompatible claim.

Both use the banyan for a lineage, but 476's image is ஆலம்வித்து, a seed of regrowth, while Naladiyar 197 is aerial roots (வீழுன்றி) propping a decaying tree; the 'prop' sense is not in 476, whose reading is flagged uncertain.

2376 has the king give wealth to the blind and abandoned, a fair case of அளி against Kural 557, but the epic has no rain image and this is illustration of a virtue; naming the sufferers adds little beyond the rule.

1320 repeats 1318's clauses (மலையெடுத்திடுவாய் ... நிகரெனக் குளரோ என்பாய்) and answers the claim of no equal, a real reply; but line 3-4 are obscure and 'the boast is what ruins him' is not in the verse. Develops fits better than tension.

139 refuses to kill for his own life; 250 says he and his mother killed a cock of flour (மாவின் நற் கோழி). The pair is real, but 'breaks the rule' is the sage's verdict that intent counts, and the marked tie between 196 and 139 (the kid is the father) is not in the Tamil of either verse.

Naladiyar 3 puts the fall in ஏனை வினை, deeds, and says nothing of neglect of rule; 297 is a usurper's murder of the king (எரியின் வாய்ப் பெய்து). Gains 'cause: the fallen king's neglect' is not in either text, and 'marked for next fall' is extrapolation.

3117 is a metaphor (கேவல மடந்தை, embrace) and ends மூழ்கினான், sunk in a sea of bliss, which is no clear 'two stay apart'; Tirumanthiram 134 (கரையற்ற சோதி கலந்த சத்து) merges. A literal reading of a metaphor; verse flagged uncertain.

354 only says the king gives up rule and, after austerity (நோற்று), rules the gods; it names no giver, and silence is not denial of grace. Tirumanthiram 634 ends ஈசன் அருளே. Different mechanism is not asserted against it.

60's blessing (உயிர்களை வருத்தஞ் செய்யாது ... அருள் பரப்பி) and Siddhar 15 (தன்னுயிர்போல் எண்ணி) share mercy to lives, but 'qualifies' is not shown, 'victims' is outside the verse, and neither side gains specifically.

139 rules out taking a life to guard one's own; 250 says they killed a flour cock (மாவினால், கொன்ற கொடுமை) and suffered every birth. The link is real, but whether this breaks 139's rule is the sage's claim, not stated by 139; weak.

963 shows welcome by embrace and seating on his elephant (தன்னொடும் ஏற்றினான்); Kural 90 is about the face changing. A shared topic of welcome, and 'a test the couplet does not set' is thin; qualifies does not fit.

252 gives the maxim in lines 3-4 (திறம் புரி கொள்கையொடு இறந்து செயின் அல்லது அரும் பொருட் கூட்டம் இருந்தோர்க்கு இல் என) matching Kural 616's effort/want, then 6-12 say her qualities (குணன்) stand between him and the work (வினை இடை விலங்கல போலும்). That marks a limit to the maxim.

1247 praises the one who ended தீராவினை; 2745 begs the teacher's அருள் to end the darkness of his own தீவினை. Same speaker, same doctrine, but one is praise and one is petition; 'develops' is only thematic and the verse flagged uncertain.
2847 lists அறிவு, காட்சி, வீரியம், இன்பம் as four; 3082 has காதிப்போர் மன்னர் fall and 'நான்மைக் கொடி' lifted. The announced four are shown attained by Civakan.

1070 shares மறந்தீர் with Kural 1316, but the inference is not the same (the Kural turns 'I thought of you' into 'forgot'; here he praises another's powder), the other woman is unnamed and the verse is flagged uncertain. 'Feigned jealousy' is not in it.

686 uses the cobra's hood-jewel (அரவின் ... படமுடை மணி); 1225 only uses the cobra for the foe's laugh as venom (நாகம் அழன்று எறி நச்சென நக்கான்). Different aspects of a stock image; 'cuts both ways' is not shown.

2025 shows the guest served and praising the food (மிகு சான்றோன்); it names neither Suramanjari's vow nor a 'poor old brahmin', and the Kural's measure by the guest's worth is not tested in it. Illustration with plot supplied from outside.

402 foretells the Kesava will take Ashvagriva's life and discus (ஆவியும் தேசறு திகரியும் வெளவுமே); 638 has Ashvagriva trust that very ஆழி to cut down the gods. The boast stands on the weapon the prophecy takes.

248 is Dharmadattan's claim that the king's ஒளி guards the world even asleep; Kural 547 makes the king's guard conditional on justice (முட்டாச் செயின்). A fair pair, but the 'king who sleeps in pleasure' (261) is outside the verse, and 'qualifies' is by the reader.

676 is an unnamed dancer's eyes and brows in one ilampakam; 2594 is Anangamalai dancing in another. 'The same art turned to a single patron' treats two different dancers as one; eyes and brows are a stock image of dance.

539 reads the planets (கோளின் சாதகம்) for the destined husband in Rajamapuram; 621 declares an hour and the merchant scatters wealth. The 'contest's hour' is the marker's reading of a flagged verse and 'staged as a decree worked out' is not in either.

247 makes the king a great deity by his power to favour or burn (அருளுமேல் அரசு ஆக்கும், காயுமேல் சுட்டிடும்); Kural 388 grants இறை to the one who does முறைசெய்து. A real contrast, but 'protect even a king who has abandoned rule' and 'why the story refutes it' are outside the verse, and இறை is not 'divinity' plainly.

In 197 the kid recalls its birth and knows its son (இசோமதி என்மகன்); Naladiyar 16's lamb nibbles the garland in the slaughter ground. 197 does not name a slaughter ground or a 'counter-case', and 'what the heedless have lost' is imported.

2442 is narrative description of painting காமவல்லி in sandal paste, with no claim, while Naladiyar 48 argues against praising sandal and garlands. A narrator's admiration is not a stated view; the 'tension' is shared topic only.

1864 has the companions fall at his feet and their grief end (அவலநோய் தீர்ந்தார்); 1741 has them resolve to search. But 1741 is spoken by Nandattan to Civakan, so a reunion has already happened, and 'the search ends here' is not clear.

Soolamani 30 names pods of ellu, avarai, tuvarai in mullai; Sirupanatruppadai 164-177 shows avarai, kayaa, kaanthal and a hunters' meal. Both are standard mullai description; 'the epic poet turned forest to farmland' and the other-side gain are unsupported.

1131 has the sage promise the yaksha's rescue and a sight after சில பகல்; 2095 has Civakan end his mother's grief by return. Fulfilment of a sort, but 'comforted by the word yet wept thin' is not in either verse and the gap is long.

198 names the seed (மெய்யறிவிலாமை) from which deeds grow and ripen into pain through births; Kural 351 says confusion (மருள்) of taking the unreal as real makes the joyless birth. The epic gives the steps of growth the couplet lacks; the couplet names the kind of knowledge lost.
108 foretells a messenger with a letter (ஓலை கொண்டு); 605 shows the king giving wealth to 'the speaker' (marker's reading: the envoy). The reward is not what 108 foretold, and arrival is not in 605.

1809 (கருமம் விளைந்தவாறு ... கூற்றமாய்) and Pazhamozhi 238 (பழவினை ... ஏவலாள் ஊருஞ் சுடும்) share the ripening deed, but the friends do not become an agent, they rejoice at the heir; the sent-servant idea is not in 1809, and its reading is open (flagged uncertain).

255 has the cocks receive அறவுமிர்தம், escape rebirth; 257 says that though the arrow kills them, 'திருவறப் பெருமையாலே' their small karmas hide and they pass to human birth. The vow explains why the death is a rebirth.

1465 turns on 'திருமகள் கணவன்', which the marker says can be the merchant's destined son-in-law; reading it as the goddess's lord (Kural 84's செய்யாள்) is a pun. The long guest-feeding is not in the verse.

Pathitruppattu 11 lines 5-6, 13 (சூருடை முழுமுதல் தடிந்த ... வேள் ... கடியுடை முழுமுதல் துமிய) set the king's felling of the guarded tree beside Murugan's; Thirumurugatruppadai 45-46, 59-60 give the god's deed (பனிக்கடல் ... சூர்முதல் தடிந்த; மாமுதல் தடிந்த). The shared phrase is a meaningful frame, though 'already signature' is a guess about dating.

695 has Arimanju plan to lure the prince to a lion (சீயந் தன்மேற் கொளப்புணர்த் திடுவன்); 1136 has him hide the lion's death. Same minister, plot sequence; 'used the king's pride' is not in 695, which names the prince's lack of judgement.

Kural 1102 makes the beloved the only cure; 1041 says the little parrot (சிறுகிளியால்) cured him. A fair contrast, but the sender is not named, the parrot is a figure of her message, and the other side gains nothing specific.
92 ranks sweet speech over a gift; 225 ranks feeding the hungry over the ascetic's endurance. They rank different pairs; 'a hungry person's view' is not in either.
